evidence.claim: SpaceX GPU lease rent is one-twentieth of financed cost per quarter plus a fixed rate, over about five years; Apollo deals total $75B versus $44.9B of neocloud chip-backed debt since 2023 (single source, The Information via FourWeekMBA).
evidence.numbers: Capital is flowing to the strongest credits (SpaceX, Anthropic) at scale while smaller neocloud credits widen.

evidence.claim: CFO: an investment-grade tenant is absolutely critical to preserve spread; Google's support for the $19bn Anthropic lease applies from lease commencement via mandatory assumption or debt-reducing termination payment, falling away on Anthropic investment-grade ratings.
evidence.numbers: Size of the support undisclosed; Justified debt not yet priced. Automated transcript.

evidence.claim: GPU debt without an investment-grade block priced at stated 9.0% and 9.51%, parent-guaranteed; non-recourse private placement stated 5.96%.
evidence.numbers: Effective rates 10.7%, 10.38% and 7.09%.

evidence.claim: CoreWeave moved certain Core Scientific leases into CW SPV, with CoreWeave still primary obligor; the 10-Q says recourse depends on its condition at default, and no analyst asked on the call.
evidence.numbers: 590 MW CoreWeave; 485 MW billing; 84% of 9M revenue; AMD over half of stabilized NOI once built.

evidence.claim: Hut 8's call named Anthropic as River Bend end user with Broadcom and Google in the credit profile; the Phase 2 lease went from 15 to 17 years to help offset financing cost.
evidence.numbers: 352 MW, $9.8bn; a longer term replaces a rent rise in the bond math.

evidence.claim: Fermi and TensorWave did not close their lease by 31 October; open conditions include construction-level project financing, guaranties and board approvals; neither party has terminated.
evidence.numbers: A signed lease with a backstopped tenant did not turn into debt; shares fell about 7% to $2.05.

evidence.claim: Cipher's Barber Lake overruns shows how lease structure allocates risk: hyperscaler leases have capex allowances, while Cipher bears the first $359.3mn at the Fluidstack site, in exchange for a 10-year AI lab term; Google's warrants carry a value test at lease commencement.
evidence.numbers: $13.0mn per IT MW vs $10.4mn; yield 15.2% with extension, 12.9% without; $435mn warrant floor, about $182mn at $6.93 (approximate).

evidence.claim: Amazon drew its $17.5bn term loan at SOFR + 0.625-0.875% and disclosed a new secured supplier loan facility of up to about $80bn for technology infrastructure, secured on purchased assets, from Q1 2027.
evidence.numbers: An AA buyer borrows near SOFR + 75bp unsecured; GPU debt without such a credit pays 11% or more. Even Amazon now pledges equipment, but its spread rests on its credit, not the asset.

evidence.claim: Microsoft launched at least $25bn of Aaa/AAA bonds in 10 tranches (2-40 years), its first US deal since 2017, a day after saying debt markets were available but 'not yet tapped'.
evidence.numbers: Initial talk T+50-55bp (2-year) to T+130-135bp (40-year), versus GPU debt without a hyperscaler wrapper at 11%+. Leases not yet commenced rose $35.5bn in one quarter to $364.6bn, so Microsoft's covenant is what landlords and neocloud lenders are underwriting.

evidence.claim: 3Q26 10-Q: data center backstops total $75.7bn: $48.0bn executed with third-party providers as credit derivatives (from $43.8bn at 30 June, $16.9bn at year-end) plus $27.7bn Google must still put in place, $10.0bn of it for Crux AI, its Blackstone joint venture.
evidence.numbers: Executed backstops up $4.2bn QoQ; the committed pipeline up $3.6bn. Terms up to 15 years, with the right to take over or sublease leases on default. No analyst asked about them on the call.

evidence.claim: Financial guarantees supporting counterparties' procurement of long-lead power equipment for Google's energy agreements rose to $16.2bn (terms to January 2049) from $7.6bn at 30 June.
evidence.numbers: More than doubled in a quarter: Google's credit now underwrites power equipment as well as leases.

evidence.claim: Asked by Morgan Stanley about customer financing strain or SRA exits, CEO said 'No' and that there is 'no change in our cash terms'; about 20% of gas customers are data centers.
evidence.numbers: SRAs fell 63 to 58 GW, but the release attributes it to 13 GW of conversions to firm orders, not exits. Current contract liabilities rose to $45.7bn: the OEM is protected by cash deposits, so tenant credit risk sits with developers and their lenders, not the supplier. Refundability of deposits is not disclosed.
evidence.source: GE Vernova 3Q26 call (single source transcript); release; 10-Q

evidence.claim: Oracle pledged to cap new capital-markets funding at $20B through May 2030; Microsoft sold $25B of bonds with orders up to $115B. (single source)
evidence.numbers: Oracle five-year CDS about 274 bps, down 22 in a day from a record 288 on 15 October; Microsoft tranches widened only 2-3 bps from issue.

evidence.claim: Galaxy declined to sign a Helios II lease over the summer because the investment-grade wrap offered did not protect both its debt and equity; it now seeks only IG hyperscalers or IG-enhanced tenants, with no fixed date.
evidence.numbers: 830 MW stays uncontracted; data halls 2028 as backstop. Landlord chose time over weaker credit while its stock trades on tenant credit.

evidence.claim: All three Helios I leases (526 MW) are with CoreWeave's parent, so Galaxy's claim sits behind site-level GPU financings; CoreWeave says the load is allocated to a large IG hyperscaler, but that can change.
evidence.numbers: Data Centers operating cash flow -$129.1mn on $79.1mn of leasing revenue (working capital -$152.2mn); cash rent not discussed on the call.

evidence.claim: Filing confirms a binding about $40B commitment: an Apollo-managed entity buys Nvidia Vera Rubin chips and leases them to SpaceX for about 5 to 5.25 years; close expected by year-end.
evidence.numbers: Rate undisclosed, so the investment-grade pricing Musk implied cannot be checked.

evidence.claim: JunkBondInvestor's Credit Weekly: the 20 AI data center high-yield bonds ($45.6B) have widened about 136 bps since mid-September and trade about 150 bps wide of single-Bs despite BB ratings. TeraWulf, with a Google backstop behind its Fluidstack rent, is tightest at 222 bps; the three landlords leasing to CoreWeave (Galaxy 788, Core Scientific 507, Applied Digital 368) widened about 150 bps in a month, twice the rest. Dispersion is explained by who pays the rent, construction progress, location and parent support.
evidence.numbers: Average spread 471 bps, average yield 9.5%, average price 93.0; all maturities 2030-31 (81% in 2031).
evidence.source: JunkBondInvestor Credit Weekly, 25 Oct 2026 (Bloomberg data as of 23 Oct)

evidence.claim: Musk says SpaceX closed $40B of GPU debt on its investment-grade rating and Starlink and launch revenue, while lenders have nearly shut out AI data center firms without other revenue.
evidence.numbers: No lenders, rates or terms given; the FT-reported Apollo package was still described as under discussion on 20 October, so the close is unconfirmed (single source).

evidence.claim: Josh preview: Google backstops neocloud leases as credit derivatives, $43.8B notional at 30 June with an estimated $24.1B more agreed in principle; at TeraWulf and Cipher about $1.3B to $1.7B per site of 168 MW or more.
evidence.numbers: The backstop is what turns a neocloud lease into financeable cash flow; Google keeps step-in and termination rights.

evidence.claim: 3Q26 10-Q: data center financing 'has generally become more difficult'; neoclouds, colocation providers and other tenants are increasingly viewed as high credit risks, which may cancel projects and push developers to negotiate lower equipment prices.
evidence.numbers: A Brookfield-affiliated financing vehicle was 26% of 3Q revenue and the largest receivable (31%); the supplier is carrying more of the working capital (contract assets $858.6mn).

evidence.claim: Meta backs two off-balance-sheet JV campuses (Louisiana/Hyperion, Texas/El Paso) with 4-year initial leases plus residual value guarantees. Partners and their lenders fund 80%, and the leases and guarantees of an AA- tenant carry the debt.
evidence.numbers: Max RVG $41.49bn at 30 Sep 2026 vs $28.09bn at YE25; total max exposure $68.40bn; development cost ~$27bn and ~$14bn.

evidence.claim: A mature, listed cloud provider signed a 10-year, 20 MW colocation lease from Q2 2027 for more than $400M over the initial term.
evidence.numbers: About $2M per MW per year on the lower figure; the article headline says $700M and does not explain the gap. Small sites can sign listed-tenant paper.

evidence.claim: The tenant's own credit is drifting: Meta had negative free cash flow, moved to net debt, and created non-voting Class C stock for capital raising, among other purposes (also employee compensation, acquisitions, general corporate purposes). Management said it has no specific financing plans.
evidence.numbers: FCF -$2.12bn; cash and securities $82.45bn vs debt $83.67bn; capex $34.91bn = 106% of OCF.

evidence.claim: FT: Anthropic is offering Blackstone more than 10% on $9B of debt backed by Anthropic's five-year chip lease payments.
evidence.numbers: Even the largest lab's lease paper prices at double digits when it is not wrapped by an investment-grade parent. Reuters could not verify (single source).
evidence.source: The Star, citing Reuters and the FT

evidence.claim: JPMorgan and Goldman guaranteed only the $1.3B lease-backed term loan in Volta's $5.0B package; the $3.7B GPU term loan was sold best-efforts.
evidence.numbers: Both loans priced at about 11.2% to 11.75% yield to maturity, per PitchBook LCD data (single source).

evidence.claim: AMD agreed credit support for TensorWave's 222 MW lease at Fermi, a chip supplier standing behind a neocloud tenant.
Wells Fargo puts AWS- or Nvidia-backed data center bonds at about 6.8–7.2% and CoreWeave- or Oracle-backed at 8–9% or more.
Project debt backed by Google-supported and investment-grade leases priced at about 6.1–6.2%.
A facility backed by three-year contracts with weaker customers priced at SOFR + 550 bps and had to widen in syndication.
Phase II notes against an unbacked CoreWeave lease priced at 9.875%, the most expensive project debt among landlords.
Josh AMZN preview: Cipher's 70 MW Stingray lease is 15-year triple-net with a 3% escalator and an Amazon.com, Inc. guarantee of rent and opex; Amazon pays overruns above $10.5M per IT MW.
evidence.numbers: The parent guarantee let Cipher raise about $810M of project debt; Josh estimates about $128 to $159 per kW-month.

evidence.claim: A facility backed by one investment-grade customer priced at SOFR + 225 bps, rated A3.

question: Does the tenant's credit, not the asset, set what developers and neoclouds pay to borrow?
summary: Every 2026 financing points the same way. Debt backed by investment-grade contracts or a hyperscaler guarantee (Google backstops, Amazon's parent guarantee at Cipher) prices near 6-7%; GPU debt without that wrapper now pays 11% or more (Volta), and even Anthropic is reported paying above 10% on lease-backed chip debt. This week SpaceX's about $40B Apollo lease confirmed Musk's claim that a borrower with non-AI revenue can still raise at scale (rate undisclosed), and Oracle's pledge to cap borrowing cut its CDS by 22 bps in a day, which shows credit now responds to balance-sheet discipline. Status unchanged.
title: Tenant credit sets the cost of capital
